content_metadata.description: An analysis of a video showcasing a hike up Mt. Baker as part of the Saranac 6er series. The video follows the narrator and John as they complete this challenging trail.

qAndA.question: What is the name of the narrow passage the hikers navigate through the rocks?

qAndA.answer: The narrator hints at a lost treasure being buried there by Native Americans. (3:12)
qAndA.question: What is the significance of the 'Devil's Fork' tree mentioned in the video?

qAndA.answer: The appearance of other hikers coming down the trail suggests they are near the top. (4:13)
qAndA.question: What visual cue indicates that the hikers are near the summit of Mt. Baker?

qAndA.answer: Hikers who complete all six peaks are supposed to ring the Saranac Lake 6er Bell, located in a gazebo in the town. (7:47)
qAndA.question: What tradition is associated with completing the Saranac Lake 6er challenge?

qAndA.answer: The narrator mentions the 'Kiwasasa curse,' which is said to bring bad luck. (8:02)
qAndA.question: What potential consequence is mentioned for those who ring the Saranac Lake 6er Bell without completing all six peaks?

youtube_description:
Jon and I hike Mt. Baker outside of Saranac Lake, NY.  This is the first (for us) in a series of six mountains that make up the Saranac 6ers Challenge. (Link below)

I apologize for the audio quality.  It may have been the rustling of the leaves (it was windy) or the new iPhone 8 plus may have some bugs.

Saranac 6er Challenge:

http://www.saranaclake.com/activities/outdoor/saranac-lake-6

Facebook: North Country Outdoor Guys

https://www.facebook.com/ncoutdoorguys/


Instagram: ncoutdoorguys
